label: PF Backlog 618
title: Split full precheck into sequential named groups (4-5) with per-group pass/fail + duration (no opaque 20-min block); add --group/--only

brief.what_adds: Sequential named groups with per-group pass/fail + duration, and --group/--only
brief.problem: Full precheck is one long opaque block with no per-step progress

objective: Split full precheck into sequential named groups (4-5) with per-group pass/fail + duration (no opaque 20-min block); add --group/--only
acceptance_criteria: Full precheck runs as named groups (structure/security/contracts/worker/backlog/quality/tests-a/tests-b/deep/release), each printing its OWN pass/fail + duration, so a failure surfaces within the first few minutes instead of after one opaque ~20-min block.
--group <name>, --only a,b and --list-groups are supported; --list-groups prints every group with its gate count or test count; the numeric aliases 1..5 still resolve (back-compat with PR#210).
--full iterates ALL named groups sequentially and prints a per-group rollup; the periodic full-tree release sweep stays behind --release (BI-PF-0385).
Every gate belongs to exactly one group and the two test halves partition the test suite (proven by unit tests).
in_scope: named-group partition of every precheck gate + the test suite
--full churns all groups with per-group rollup
approach: Add a NAMED group map (_GROUP_OF/_GROUP_ORDER) partitioning every _GATES entry plus the test suite (tests-a/tests-b halves), and a runner (_run_groups) that emits per-group PASS/FAIL + duration + a rollup. main() routes --group/--only/--list-groups and makes --full iterate the groups (release excluded). Numeric aliases 1..5 retained. Also restore the scoped-tests walk shadowed by PR#210's duplicate _test_files.
verification: python -m compileall clean; wired_audit OK (0 unwired)
risks: pre-existing test_backlog_dod failures are unrelated (fail on clean develop); release sweep kept out of --full per BI-PF-0385

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the existing config/plan-groups.json as the single source for group membership; extend the precheck runner to iterate groups sequentially, emit per-group pass/fail + duration, and parse --group/--only flags. Reuse existing engineering gate endpoints for result reporting instead of new ones.
conflict_findings: BI-0184 touches the same quality-gate execution path; coordinate group definitions vs run-mode profiles.
BI-PF-1336 may change which groups run on change vs schedule.
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1336 overlaps on CI gating but targets per-change vs scheduled cadence; this item is the grouping primitive it would reuse.
BI-0184 run-mode-aware gate must be expressed as a group/profile mapping, not reimplemented.
analysis.rationale: Existing plan-groups config and gate endpoints make this an additive EXTEND; groups are the reusable primitive that BI-PF-1336 and BI-0184 both need.
assumptions: config/plan-groups.json already models grouping and can be extended with ordering + mandatory flags.
Current precheck is invoked via a single CLI entry point that can be refactored into a group loop without behavior change.
Existing gate/fail endpoints are sufficient for per-group result recording.
risks: Group boundaries may not match real dependency order, causing skipped-but-required checks.
Per-group duration reporting could add noise or slow the runner.
--only could let users bypass mandatory safety groups.
evidence: Candidate module config/plan-groups.json exists as grouping config.
Candidate APIs /engineering/assignments/{item_id}/fail and /pidl/consequential show existing gate/report paths.
missing_info: Exact names and membership of the 4-5 groups (final list needs human confirmation).
Whether --only may exclude mandatory groups or is advisory-only.
Whether per-group results must persist to the API or are console/CI-output only.
Default behavior when no --group flag is given (full sequential run vs prior behavior).

context_review.reason: Only a repeated one-line objective; no named groups, no approach details (CLI wiring, output format), and no affected files/components specified.

api_impact.reason: developer tooling (CLI); no HTTP surface, no customer-visible runtime
